title: Tanzanian Beef Stir Fry
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Beef Stir Fry — tender beef strips stir-fried at maximum heat with mixed vegetables, garlic, ginger, and Tanzanian spices in a quickly made bold sauce. Fast, vibrant, and full of flavour — the quick dinner of urban Tanzania.
longDesc: Beef stir fry is the dish that Dar es Salaam's quick-service restaurants do best — thin beef strips at screaming-hot heat, a few vegetables, and a bold quick sauce. In and out of the pan in 15 minutes but with flavour that takes much longer to build in a slow dish.
steps: Heat wok to smoking over highest heat.
Add oil. Sear beef in two batches — 1.5—2 minutes. Remove.
Add carrots and peppers. Stir-fry 2 minutes.
Return beef. Add ginger, soy, oyster sauce, cumin, paprika.
Toss everything together on high heat for 2 minutes.
chefTips: Maximum heat throughout — this is a stir-fry.
Small batches for beef — crowding produces steaming.
Everything prepped before starting — it moves fast.
cookingScience: See TZA031 for stir-fry science. This version uses even higher heat (wok) and less sauce, producing a drier, more charred result called "wok hei" — the characteristic breath of the wok.
sustainabilityTips: Mixed vegetables reduce total beef quantity needed.
culturalNote: Beef stir fry reflects Tanzania's openness to cooking techniques from the Indian Ocean trading world — Chinese cooking methods arrived on the East African coast centuries ago and have become completely naturalised.
